newsitem.title: UK: Sears bounces as Littlewoods restarts talks.
newsitem.headline: Sears bounces as Littlewoods restarts talks.

text.p: Shares in retailer Sears Plc bounced after an early fall on Wednesday as the company announced it had re-entered talks with Littlewoods on the sale of Sears' home shopping business Freemans, dealers said.
Earlier, the shares slid on news that N. Brown Group Plc had pulled out of negotiations to buy Freemans.
Sears shares were 1/2p firmer at 76-1/2 by 0900 GMT after falling to a low of 72. N. Brown shares climbed 19p to 396-1/2.

In January, Littlewoods LWD.CN agreed to buy Freemans for 395 million stg, but the acquisition was referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission on competition grounds. Littlewoods then withdrew from the deal when it emerged that Sears was talking to other possible buyers.
N. Brown emerged as the favourite to buy the company, but then announced that "after due diligence, N. Brown felt unable to proceed."
Sears said it had re-entered talks with Littlewoods, but Littlewoods said only that it may re-open talks if it got exclusivity.
"It's very worrying," one dealer said. "People don't know what's behind N. Brown pulling out. There could be other problems lurking behind it."
